about: Selection facts for the appendix tables of scripts/paper_appendix.py: the ACL Anthology export that defines the corpus (record counts, SHA-256, date range, in-scope records per year), the eligibility criteria E1-E5, the screening rubric A-F, the 24 selected papers in selection order (hard-case flag, venue, screening scores A-F, base score A+B+C+D+F), the screened near-misses and the language-based exclusions.
criteria: the selected output is from a fixed label set, predefined scale, candidate set, or supplied ranking set.
this component is central enough that replacing it tests a substantive prediction claim.
same fixed split and primary metric, or a close reconstruction.
label inventory and input are defined well enough to prompt a model.
evaluation text, labels and protocol are released or credibly reconstructable.

near.name: FRANQ
near.status: Near-miss / **E5 pending**: public code found, custom long-form annotated test files not verified.

near.name: LATTE
near.status: Eligible on reconstructed samples but weaker dedicated artifacts, less distinctive stress.

near.name: QC-NLI
near.status: Eligible but redundant with MISMATCHED and INLI. GPT-4o conversions add label-quality variation.

near.name: Entangled Relations / MetaEntail-RE
near.status: Near-miss: useful but overlaps Entity or Relation Embeddings and NLI, and variable candidate lists require protocol-specific freezing.

near.name: DISARM
near.status: Near-miss: high-quality relation task, but stance/argument coverage overlaps EZ-STANCE and relation coverage.

near.name: Few-shot Prompting for Pairwise Ranking
near.status: Eligible, but PRP-Graph already covers finite-candidate ranking with less overlap in method.

near.name: Pairwise Ranking Prompting
near.status: Eligible, but near duplicate of PRP-Graph/Few-shot PRP.

near.name: LINKAGE
near.status: Eligible, but the sampled train queries and generated reference answers make it less clean than PRP-Graph.

near.name: SCOOS
near.status: Eligible but repository is a “code soon” placeholder. CICC and Navigating cover intent/OOD with stronger artifacts.

near.name: GUM-SAGE
near.status: Eligible but near-miss: useful ordinal/ranking task with small test-document count and proxy targets.

near.name: CREHate
near.status: Near-miss: there is no held-out test, evaluation uses all posts, and a sample-level language filter was not established.

near.name: MAVEN-FACT
near.status: **E5 fails**: test set withheld for online scoring. Not a local reproducible test.

near.name: SAFARI
near.status: **E5 fails**: article text is not released, and reconstruction requires scraping.

near.name: Accurate and Data-Efficient Toxicity Prediction when Annotators Disagree
near.status: **E5 fails**: cited dataset is encrypted/password-gated, with no verified public code/data route.

near.name: FactAppeal
near.status: **E2 fails**: target labels are source/evidence features rather than truth/factuality verdict, and there is no verified code/data link.

near.name: FactSelfCheck
near.status: Near-miss: evaluation depends on claim/triple extraction and multiple generations, and the fixed bounded decision is not the whole proposed method.

near.name: Factcheck-Bench / VeriScore
near.status: **E1 fails for the full method**: open claim extraction and evidence retrieval are bundled with verdict prediction.

near.name: PrefixNLI
near.status: Conditional near-miss: only the explicitly English slice could be considered, and the exact held-out count was not established.

near.name: LegalLens: Leveraging LLMs for Legal Violation Identification in Unstructured Text
near.status: Near-miss: exact closed label inventory and held-out split were not established in the screen. Counted separately from the workshop shared-task paper.

near.name: LegalLens Shared Task 2024
near.status: Excluded by venue rule (workshop), and the held-out test N was not reported.

near.name: PILOT: Legal Case Outcome Prediction with Case Law
near.status: Excluded under the strict source-data rule: summaries do not establish that the underlying dataset is English-only, and the paper does not report a verified English-only source-document split.

near.name: Better Call CLAUSE
near.status: Eligible on the bounded discrepancy-label slice, but a near-miss because the broader benchmark also asks for open-ended explanations/citations and legal coverage is already represented by LegalSeg.

near.name: SenseRel
near.status: Eligible but lower priority: small evaluation sets and overlaps graded semantic relation tasks.

near.name: VariErr NLI
near.status: Eligible but less direct replacement target: verdict concerns explanation validity, not the underlying language task, and a near-miss to NLI/factuality.

near.name: LCES
near.status: Eligible but no official code link found and ASAP evaluation N is not stated exactly. DREsS has clearer rubric/task and release.

near.name: Thought Trees for Science Question Scoring
near.status: Eligible with public code/data, but synthetic rationale preferences and API-generated data make the training method less clean for this replacement question.

near.name: OPINE
near.status: Conditional language/artifact near-miss: the underlying papers are English, but the official repository says code/documentation will be released later.

near.name: BESSTIE
near.status: Excluded: the full test release breaks the English-only rule, because its Indian Reddit portion contains code-mixing (mean English probability 0.87). A separately released English-only subset could be reconsidered.

near.name: DIA-HARM
near.status: Conditional language exclusion: the 50-variety set includes Patois, and there is no separately released standard-English-only split.

near.name: DynaCounter
near.status: English dataset, but its central contribution is counterspeech generation, not a bounded predictor replacement.

near.name: SGToxicGuard
near.status: Conditional: potentially usable as an English-file carve-out, but schema and exact task slice require confirmation, and other languages are excluded.

near.name: Leveraging Codebook Knowledge with NLI and ChatGPT for Zero-Shot Political Relation Classification
near.status: Language boundary unresolved in the screen, so it is held out until the source-example language is verified.

near.name: Rethinking STS and NLI in Large Language Models
near.status: Paper-wide results are excluded, but an explicitly isolated English-only dataset row could be assessed separately.

near.name: EVADE: LLM-Based Explanation Generation and Validation for Error Detection in NLI
near.status: Language and bounded-task boundary unresolved, so not in core.

near.name: A RelEntLess Benchmark for Modelling Graded Relations between Named Entities
near.status: Eligible but not selected: useful graded relation geometry, though ranking/scalar coverage is already supplied by PRP-Graph, Scalar Constructs and DREsS.

near.name: Improving Quotation Attribution with Fictional Character Embeddings
near.status: Near-miss: long-novel context is useful, but upstream quote detection, coreference and candidate-speaker construction complicate faithful replacement.

near.name: Revisiting Supertagging for Faster HPSG Parsing
near.status: Eligible in principle, but near-miss due to a specialist grammar inventory and sequential constraints, and less directly comparable with a simple per-instance classifier.

near.name: Exploring the Potential of ChatGPT on Sentence Level Relations
near.status: Eligible only on its English subsets (TB-Dense, MATRES, TDDMan); a near-miss because its DiscoGeM set is multilingual and ConTempo covers temporal classification with a more direct proposed predictor.

near.name: Putting Context in Context: The Impact of Discussion Structure on Text Classification
near.status: Eligible, but a near-miss because it adds little beyond the relation/stance families already in core.

near.name: Human Temporal Inferences Go Beyond Aspectual Class
near.status: Near-miss pending PDF-level split and label-scale confirmation: a public dataset is noted, but the exact comparable test protocol was not established.

near.name: Emotion Dynamics
near.status: **E3 fails for this audit:** aggregate time-series analysis, no fixed bounded supervised test split.

near.name: How DDAIR You? Disambiguated Data Augmentation for Intent Recognition
near.status: Near-miss: central claim is data augmentation, not replacement of a fixed task predictor.

near.name: Can LLMs Reason Like Doctors?
near.status: Near-miss: evaluation study across mixed QA tasks rather than a central proposed bounded predictor.

near.name: RiTeK
near.status: Near-miss: candidate set/output cardinality is not clearly closed, so E1 is unclear.

langex: INJONGO (16 African languages), ViGoEmotions (Vietnamese), BanTH (Romanized Bangla), MiLiC-Eval (Tibetan/Uyghur/Kazakh/Mongolian), IrokoBench/AfriXNLI (17 African languages), K-LJP (Chinese legal text), Icelandic Clinical Coding, SinhalaMMLU, LaoBench, Italian legal rhetorical-role classification, and SememeLRM/HowNet (Chinese).

MCN (18 languages), Better as Generators Than Classifiers (11 languages), Macaron (20 languages/dialects), ConLID (2,099 language/script labels), CommonLID (109-way language identification), SIB-200 (205 varieties), SemRel2024 (13 languages), DISRPT discourse corpora (13 languages), Babel-670 (30 scripts), Taxi1500 (1,504 languages), UniversalCEFR (13 languages), MultiFED (Indic datasets), MMLU-ProX (29 languages), M-RewardBench (23 languages), ReMedy (39 translation language pairs), PEAR (multilingual MT), and Bi-STANCE (Chinese/English).

ShieldLM (English/Chinese), CrisisTS (English/French), NaijaHate, RAGTruthPrefixes (English/Chinese), COMI-LINGUA (Hindi-English code mix), MoVa (“primarily English,” not uniformly), and English-containing multilingual QE work such as BoostedProb, Sigmoid Head for Quality Estimation under Language Ambiguity, and Watching the Watchers.
